title: Clarify interactive role mapping and contrast ramp for dense data controls
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
We discovered a set of borderline accessibility issues in dense data controls (compact tables, filter chips, dense pagination and mini-toolbar actions, and several chart legends). Problems include inconsistent ARIA roles on chips and badges, ambiguous focus order in compact table rows with inline actions, and color token choices that do not meet contrast thresholds at small sizes or when used in disabled/hover states. This ticket scopes design-level remediation: update role/aria guidance, produce a contrast token ramp for data components, and provide interaction specs for keyboard navigation when table row density is high.

Goal:
- Produce final design decisions and token recommendations that engineering can implement in a single pass for the 2026.03 design release.
- Ensure components pass VPAT procedural checks for keyboard and perceivable color contrast in common usage patterns.

Out of scope:
- Implementation work in code (handled by ENG tickets).
- Full rework of component anatomy beyond density-related touchpoints.
tasks: Audit: enumerate component instances where current tokens fail 4.5:1 or 3:1 (text vs UI) at 12px/14px sizes
Define: new contrast token ramp for data surfaces (data-surface-01..04) and action tokens (action-compact/hover/disabled)
Spec: ARIA role mapping for chips/badges (button vs switch vs link) and recommended aria-label/aria-describedby patterns
UX flow: keyboard traversal for compact table rows with inline menus and focus-visible styles
Create: Figma frames showing before/after token swaps for charts, small text labels, and disabled states
Document: VPAT checklist entries and sample test steps for QA to verify keyboard and contrast conformance
acceptance_criteria: Design token document updated with named tokens and example usage for dense data controls
Figma spec with annotated interaction states, focus rings, and aria notes merged to DS library
Clear mapping table: component -> recommended role -> aria attributes (examples)
Conformance checklist drafted for QA and Accessibility Ops with reproducible test steps
Hand-off notes with sample CSS variables and example token values for ENG ticket creation
comments: 2026-02-11 - Aisha Patel: Initial audit complete. Found 14 instances where color contrast for secondary text falls below 4.5:1 at 12px on data-surface-02. Compounded by dark-mode inversion causing label legibility issues in charts.

2026-02-18 - Sofia García: Proposed token ramp attached in Figma. Suggests increasing contrast for data-label-medium and adding a new token data-action-compact-hover. Marking some chart palette swatches as 'use with caution' for small labels.

2026-02-24 - Design review: Marcus Liu and Priya Nair reviewed ARIA mapping. Decision: treat chips with toggle behavior as role='switch' with aria-checked; chips that open a menu become role='button' with aria-expanded. Update guidance for screen reader announcement order.

2026-03-03 - Accessibility review (external consultant): Recommended stronger focus-visible outline for compact rows to maintain 3:1 contrast against hovered background. Also recommended testing NVDA/VoiceOver with dense table examples.

2026-03-08 - Sofia García: Figma updated — added step-through keyboard prototype demonstrating Tab, ArrowLeft/Right, Enter for chips and TableRow focus movement. Pushed notes into DS library components (awaiting engineering implementation).
2026-03-12 - Aisha Patel: Drafted VPAT checklist for the scoped items and added example test steps. Next: create ENG tickets for token substitutions and keyboard behavior changes.
notes: Trade-offs considered: we can either keep token names stable and change values (preferred for low friction) or add new token names scoped to dense controls (clearer for future but costlier to update).
We chose to add a small set of new tokens (data-surface-03, data-action-compact-hover) to avoid regressions in other components that rely on existing token semantics.
Engineering will need a small migration plan: CSS var mapping and runtime feature flag to roll out token swaps gradually across apps. Add ENG ticket linking to runtime-1.18 migration plan.
next_steps: Create ENG tickets for: token swaps, focus-visible style changes, and ARIA attribute enforcement (estimated 2 sprint work).
Schedule paired review with Accessibility Engineer for implementation smoke tests (target week 2026-W12).
Finalize VPAT checklist and attach to the design handoff doc for QA signoff.
